*Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa says she has not spoken with Elon Musk but is open to working with him after he described her as “quite moderate” and predicted she would be “fine” as governor.*

• *Musk:* Hinojosa acknowledged his significant business interests in Texas and said cooperation must benefit Texans.
• *Political Identity:* Asked whether she is a moderate, Hinojosa rejected ideological labels, saying, “If I had to label myself, I'd call myself an economic populist.”
• *Corporate Influence:* She argued that corporate interests have corrupted both political parties and called for leaders who prioritize constituents over corporate pressure.
• *Economic Priorities:* Hinojosa said Texas can maintain a strong business community, but its economy must serve residents first.

Lumentum *($LITE)* CEO Michael Hurlston defended its planned $115B all-stock merger with Marvell *($MRVL)* after shares plunged 42% and 45%, respectively, since Oct. 28, acknowledging shareholder frustration but citing strong AI demand.

• *Deal Outlook:* Announced Nov. 2, the merger is expected to close in H1 2028. The $115B figure represented Lumentum’s implied enterprise value at announcement.
• *Growth Driver:* Hurlston sees the shift from copper to fiber-optic connections inside AI data centers as a major opportunity, with no slowdown in Lumentum’s demand.
• *Investor Concerns:* Both stocks have suffered from merger skepticism and broader AI valuation pressure. Hurlston acknowledged, “We’ve got work to do with our shareholders.”
• *Upcoming Catalysts:* Marvell’s Dec. 1 earnings, the merger’s S-4 filing and Lumentum’s next earnings report could help rebuild investor confidence.
• *Financial Strength:* Lumentum’s latest quarterly revenue more than doubled year over year, beating expectations. Hurlston said both businesses are performing strongly.

SpaceX lenders sought to prevent Elon Musk from launching Nvidia *($NVDA)* AI chips securing a $43B debt package into orbit, fearing the collateral would be impossible to recover in a default, according to people familiar with the deal.

• *Project Saturn:* SpaceX sold more than $30B in debt Thursday, including $25B in investment-grade bonds backed by five-year lease payments on Nvidia Vera Rubin GPUs.
• *Orbital Restrictions:* Lenders proposed prohibiting the launch of pledged chips as Musk pursues space-based AI data centers. It remains unclear whether the restriction was included in final documents.
• *Bond Terms:* The $25B tranche carries an estimated 8.3% yield, or 3.45 percentage points above Treasuries. Bonds mature in 2032, with principal scheduled for repayment in under four years.
• *Credit Structure:* Debt was issued through a special-purpose vehicle to preserve SpaceX’s investment-grade rating. Moody’s rated the debt A3 and KBRA A-, supported by binding lease payments.
• *Investors:* Pimco committed $4B, with BlackRock, Goldman Sachs Asset Management and KKR also participating. Apollo and Goldman Sachs led the deal.
• *Deployment:* Moody’s says the GPUs are intended for SpaceX-controlled U.S. data centers on Earth, not orbital facilities.

*Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa reaffirmed plans to ban new data center permits when she takes office in January, clarifying that projects already approved would not be frozen.*

• *Moratorium:* Hinojosa told Bret Baier she would block new permits within her authority until Texas passes stronger protections for residents.
• *Industry Position:* “I don't hate data centers; I just hate the way they're taking advantage of Texans right now.”
• *Existing Projects:* “I don't think I have power to stop what's already been done,” she said, distinguishing previously approved projects from pending applications.
• *Local Control:* Hinojosa wants communities to have a say in whether and how data centers are built near them.
• ⁠*The proposal comes as Texas regulators have resumed issuing data center air permits ahead of her inauguration.*

*Multiple cyberattacks and data breaches were reported worldwide Thursday, Nov. 19, as the NSA’s classified communications network remained disrupted for a third day. U.S. officials say there is no evidence linking the NSA outage to a cyberattack or the recent wave of infrastructure failures.*

• *NSA Network:* NSANet disruptions affected intelligence operations supporting the Middle East, forcing personnel to use backup communications. Officials attributed the outage to software updates, not malicious activity.
• *U.S. Banking:* JPMorgan Chase *($JPM)*, Visa *($V)* and Mastercard *($MA)* disclosed cyberattacks involving third-party vendors that exposed some customer information. Their core payment networks were not compromised.
• *Nvidia:* *($NVDA)* is investigating claims by the Gentlemen ransomware group, which threatened to release data Nov. 28. Nvidia found no evidence its own networks were breached but is investigating a possible third-party incident.
• *European Commission:* Officials confirmed an AI-assisted cyberattack targeting internal systems. The investigation remains ongoing.
• *Norwegian Energy:* Equinor confirmed its cyberattack remained ongoing Thursday, while Skagerak Energi separately reported an attempted intrusion. Energy production was unaffected.
• *VMware:* Google researchers disclosed Chinese-linked exploitation of a critical vCenter vulnerability dating to September. Broadcom issued emergency patches Thursday.
• *Additional Breaches:* Japan’s SBC Medical Group disclosed exposure of 1.6M customer records, while Ethiopian Airlines investigated a breach involving its ShebaMiles loyalty program.

*Global markets extended their selloff into Friday’s Asian session, with Japan and South Korea plunging over 4%, gold falling below $3,550, silver below $42 and Bitcoin nearing $61,000. Rising Fed rate-hike expectations, AI valuation concerns and broad risk reduction are intensifying pressure across asset classes.*

• *U.S. Markets:* The Dow plunged 1,101 points Thursday to 49,097, its first close below 50,000 since June. The S&P 500 lost 2.02% and Nasdaq fell 2.25%, despite Anthropic’s record IPO.
• *Asian Selloff:* Japan’s Nikkei and South Korea’s KOSPI dropped over 4%. SoftBank plunged roughly 16%, while SK Hynix and Samsung fell sharply as selling spread across AI and semiconductor stocks.
• *Gold & Silver:* Precious metals extended their decline to multimonth lows. A stronger dollar, expectations of further Fed tightening and possible margin-related selling are outweighing safe-haven demand.
• *Bitcoin:* BTC traded near $61,700 as U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs continued experiencing withdrawals. Funds recorded $306.5M in net outflows Nov. 18, including $148.7M from BlackRock’s IBIT.
• *Federal Reserve:* Markets are pricing another December rate hike following hawkish Fed minutes. The dollar reached a 19-month high, increasing pressure on non-yielding assets and leveraged investments.

*White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was fired, CBS News reports, contradicting earlier accounts describing his departure as amicable. The dismissal comes amid widespread U.S. technology outages and growing concerns about cybersecurity readiness.*

• *Dismissal:* White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller reportedly wanted Cairncross removed from his first day in the role, questioning whether he had the cybersecurity expertise needed for the position.
• *Replacement:* Pentagon Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies will replace Cairncross. Reuters reports she will initially serve in an acting capacity.
• *Infrastructure Outages:* The departure follows disruptions affecting Microsoft, air traffic control, banks and the NSA. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said investigators found no evidence the outages were connected and was “98% confident” they were not caused by malicious foreign activity.

*The U.S. Senate just passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) in a 62–33 vote Thursday, advancing a major overhaul of federal energy permitting aimed at accelerating power generation, transmission infrastructure and grid expansion as AI data center electricity demand surges.*

• *Faster Permitting:* The bill streamlines federal environmental reviews for power plants, transmission lines, pipelines and other infrastructure, while reducing many legal challenge windows to 150 days.
• *Data Center Costs:* New data centers of all sizes would be required to cover the additional grid infrastructure costs they create, rather than passing those expenses to households and other electricity customers.
• *Financial Protections:* Data center operators would face financial guarantees and continued payment obligations to protect ratepayers if facilities shut down before related infrastructure costs are recovered.
• *Power Grid Expansion:* Federal regulators would gain broader authority to approve certain interstate transmission lines, potentially accelerating electricity delivery to AI campuses and other high-demand regions.
• *Community Oversight:* The bill would establish federal technical assistance for local governments evaluating data center electricity demand, water use, infrastructure costs and economic impacts.
• *White House Support:* Trump endorsed BAAJA as advancing his “America First Energy Agenda,” while the White House formally declared strong support for its passage and recommended presidential approval.
• *Next Steps:* The Senate-amended bill heads to the House, which must approve the same text before it reaches Trump for his signature.

*Taiwan stocks are on track for their worst week since 1991 as the global AI selloff intensifies despite government intervention. The Taiex plunged as much as 6.4% Friday, extending weekly losses beyond 17% amid mounting margin calls and forced selling.*

• *AI Selloff:* Technology stocks account for over 70% of the Taiex, leaving Taiwan heavily exposed to the AI downturn. Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO failed to restore confidence, with shares falling 4.7% in U.S. after-hours trading.
• *Forced Liquidations:* Barclays analysts identified retail margin-related selling as a major driver of Monday’s plunge, warning that continued deleveraging could intensify losses.
• *Government Intervention:* Taiwan tightened short-selling restrictions for the second time this month, reducing intraday borrowed-share short orders to 1% of a stock’s 30-day average volume, down from 3%. Certain hedging and market-making activities remain exempt.
• *Market Pressure:* Aggregate short interest stood at 5.28% of float Thursday, versus 5.49% on Nov. 6, according to S3 Partners. The Taiex has lost over 25% since its Oct. 6 record, reducing its year-to-date gain to roughly 25%.
• *Investor Concerns:* UOB Kay Hian’s Steven Leung said mounting margin calls are forcing further deleveraging, while short sellers show little urgency to cover.

*Anthropic ($ANT) shares plunged more than 10% in premarket trading Friday, their second day on Nasdaq, as a global AI selloff overshadowed its record IPO. Elevated valuations, competitive threats and concerns over AI infrastructure financing weighed on sentiment.*

• *Global Selloff:* MSCI's Asia-Pacific index fell 3.3% to its lowest since April, putting global equities on course for their longest losing streak since September 2023. Nasdaq-100 futures dropped 1.8%.
• *AI Concerns:* Investors remain uneasy about semiconductor valuations, AI financing and Nvidia's ($NVDA) role in supporting the industry following its longtime CEO's departure. Potential regulatory changes following the Democratic midterm sweep could also complicate data-center approvals.
• *Market Sentiment:* Reed Capital CIO Gerald Gan described sentiment as deeply pessimistic and warned against buying too early. Tandem Investment Advisors' Jordan Watson called Anthropic a key real-time indicator of the broader AI risk trade.

*Anthropic ($ANT) completed a record-breaking stock market debut, with its IPO and concurrent private placement totaling $119.5B for the company and selling co-founders. The offering surpassed SpaceX's previous $86.25B IPO record set in June.*

• *Offering Breakdown:* The total comprised $93.5B from the IPO, including additional shares sold through the underwriters' over-allotment option, and $26B from a concurrent private placement.
• *Potential Index Demand:* Anthropic could join the Russell 1000 and Nasdaq-100 as early as December if it qualifies under accelerated inclusion rules, potentially attracting billions in index-fund purchases.
• *Management Outlook:* CFO Krishna Rao said raising nearly $120B leaves Anthropic well positioned to pursue opportunities regardless of market volatility.

*Anthropic ($ANT) shares plunged more than 9% in premarket trading Friday, their second day on Nasdaq, as a global AI selloff overshadowed its record IPO. Elevated valuations, competitive threats and concerns over AI infrastructure financing weighed on sentiment.*

• *Global Selloff:* MSCI's Asia-Pacific index fell 3.3% to its lowest since April, putting global equities on course for their longest losing streak since September 2023. Nasdaq-100 futures dropped 1.8%.
• *AI Concerns:* Investors remain uneasy about semiconductor valuations, AI financing and Nvidia's ($NVDA) role in supporting the industry following its longtime CEO's departure. Potential regulatory changes following the Democratic midterm sweep could also complicate data-center approvals.
• *Market Sentiment:* Reed Capital CIO Gerald Gan described sentiment as deeply pessimistic and warned against buying too early. Tandem Investment Advisors' Jordan Watson called Anthropic a key real-time indicator of the broader AI risk trade.

*The U.S. and Israel are considering a near-term assault on Iran, sources told CBS News. Netanyahu favors a joint operation, but Trump has not decided whether or how to strike.*

• *Israeli Concerns:* Netanyahu fears Iran is rapidly rebuilding ballistic missile production and moving military and nuclear infrastructure underground. Israel's military is prepared for renewed fighting and remains on heightened defensive alert.
• *Weapons Concerns:* Trump alleged Iran may be developing chemical or biological weapons without providing evidence. Tehran rejected the claims, comparing them to allegations preceding the 2003 Iraq invasion. International monitors believe roughly 900 pounds of 60%-enriched uranium remain buried at damaged nuclear sites, though Iran denies seeking nuclear weapons.
• *Recent Escalation:* The U.S. struck Iran's Qeshm Island Tuesday, citing self-defense after Iranian strikes targeting U.S. assets in Bahrain, which American forces said they intercepted. Iran also struck Kuwait this week, reportedly causing no damage.
• *Political Pressure:* Netanyahu could lose power within weeks as rivals seek to form a government following October's election. Democrats take control of both chambers of Congress in January, gaining greater influence over war funding. The conflict remains deeply unpopular among Americans.

*South Korea’s SK Hynix plans to become the largest shareholder in Japanese NAND rival Kioxia by converting bonds into equity in December, securing an indirect stake of approximately 14.1% as AI data center demand drives memory-chip growth, Reuters reports.*

• *Transaction:* SK Hynix will convert bonds into 129,000 common shares of an investment vehicle and purchase another 1,001 shares from Bain Capital, giving it indirect ownership in Kioxia.
• *Ownership Plans:* SK Hynix has no immediate plans to buy or sell additional Kioxia shares, and its involvement in management will remain limited.
• *NAND Market:* SK Hynix ranks second globally with 19% market share, while Kioxia ranks fourth with 14%, according to Counterpoint Research.
• *AI Demand:* Strong demand for NAND storage across smartphones, servers and AI data centers provides a favorable backdrop for both companies.
• *Investment History:* SK Hynix invested ¥395B ($2.48B) in the Bain-led acquisition of Toshiba Memory in 2018. Kioxia subsequently listed in Tokyo in December 2024.

NextEra Energy *($NEE)* cleared a major antitrust hurdle in its proposed $66.8B acquisition of Dominion Energy *($D)*, advancing a utility merger aimed at expanding electricity infrastructure amid surging AI data center demand.

• *Regulatory Approval:* The DOJ closed its investigation after NextEra agreed to five years of independent oversight of certain power-plant closures to protect electricity competition and costs.
• *Energy Expansion:* The combined utility would serve roughly 10M customer accounts with 110 GW of generation capacity, targeting approximately $59B in annual infrastructure investment from 2027–2032.
• *Deal Terms:* Dominion shareholders would receive 0.8138 NextEra shares per share, plus a share of $360M in cash.
• *Next Steps:* Federal energy, nuclear and state approvals remain pending, with closing expected in H2 2027.

*China’s sovereign wealth fund, China Investment Corporation (CIC), is seeking to resume investments in U.S. private equity funds, but wants protections against escalating U.S.-China tensions and potential Western sanctions, the Financial Times reports.*

• *Investment Conditions:* CIC is negotiating special terms allowing private equity funds to cash out Chinese investors if U.S. or European sanctions threaten their holdings.
• *Market Impact:* A deal could help revive U.S. private equity fundraising from Chinese institutional investors after years of geopolitical uncertainty.
• *Investment History:* Founded in 2007 to diversify China's foreign reserves, CIC previously invested in Morgan Stanley *($MS)* and Blackstone *($BX)*, exiting Blackstone in 2018.

*Trump will hold a White House news conference Friday at 12 PM ET following his Asia trip, amid renewed Iran war tensions, economic concerns and political uncertainty after Democrats won control of Congress.*

• *Trade & China:* Trump plans to discuss agreements with Thailand, the Philippines and other countries, alongside his summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
• *Iran:* Questions are expected over potential additional U.S. strikes and stalled ceasefire negotiations. Trump has recently sent mixed signals about further military action.

Ondas *($ONDS)*, Palantir *($PLTR)* and Regna AI hosted an invitation-only defense technology summit Nov. 18, focused on accelerating deployment of AI, autonomous systems and advanced manufacturing for military operations.

• *Defense AI:* Palantir demonstrated sovereign AI for mission-critical operations, emphasizing military control over sensitive data and systems. The company described its partnership with Ondas and Regna AI as expanding.
• *Autonomous Systems:* Discussions covered unmanned air and maritime platforms, scaling production, Pentagon partnerships and defense investment.
• *Formula One Partnership:* Ondas announced a “Speed to Decision” Global Partner relationship with Aston Martin’s F1 team. Aston Martin Performance Technologies shared rapid-manufacturing and supply-chain techniques applicable to defense production.
• *Industry Outlook:* Ondas CEO Eric Brock highlighted growing demand and investment in companies combining AI, autonomy and scalable manufacturing.

Hunterbrook Media says Congress released previously confidential details of Nvidia *($NVDA)* and AMD *($AMD)* AI chip export applications to China just hours after its investigation was published. House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast said withholding the information would be “contrary to the national interest.”

• *Congressional Disclosure:* Records show 3.44M advanced AI chips requested for China, with 879,868 approved across 21 applications as of May 11, 2026.
• *Chinese Buyers:* Approved licenses included chips for Alibaba, Tencent, Baidu and BYD, companies designated by the Pentagon as Chinese military companies.
• *Export Concerns:* Nvidia applications named potential intermediaries that raised chip-diversion concerns. Both Nvidia and AMD assessed diversion risks as low.
• *Shipment Status:* Approved chips were listed as unshipped as of May 11. The disclosures do not establish illegal exports or confirm subsequent deliveries.

• Nvidia’s filings name Maginfra. Hunterbrook found near-identical AMD firmware there and at blacklisted IEIT. Chip diversion remains unproven.

*SpaceX-owned Cursor is considering phasing out Chinese-developed AI models over geopolitical risks, according to a congressional report obtained by CNBC, as Washington scrutinizes growing U.S. reliance on Chinese AI technology.*

• *Chinese AI Dependence:* Cursor built its Composer 2 coding model on Moonshot AI’s Kimi K2.5. SpaceX acquired Cursor in August at an implied $60B valuation and has involved it in training Grok models.
• *Competitive Advantage:* The House investigation found Chinese open-weight models are gaining adoption through lower costs, customization and near-frontier performance, with U.S. alternatives struggling to compete.
• *Congressional Response:* Lawmakers recommend a national American open-weight AI initiative and expanding federal restrictions on Chinese-developed models to government systems and contracts.
• *Broader Scrutiny:* Airbnb and DoorDash also participated in the investigation. Separately, U.S. regulators introduced new restrictions Monday targeting Chinese companies’ remote access to advanced AI chips.

*Citigroup warns U.S. interest rates are "unsustainably high" as falling stock valuations and weaker AI investment threaten growth, potentially pushing the Fed toward rate cuts in 2027.*

• *Rate Outlook:* Citi expects a 25-basis-point hike in December 2026, a pause in early 2027 and rate cuts later that year.
• *Fed Policy:* Despite persistent inflation concerns, Citi sees aggressive hikes as unlikely during a stock-market selloff.
• *Potential Shift:* Tighter financial conditions, weakening AI investment and easing energy prices could eventually outweigh inflation risks, prompting a more dovish Fed stance.

Wall Street strategists warn that Nvidia *($NVDA)* earnings and Anthropic *($ANT)*’s record IPO failed to revive investor confidence, as AI financing concerns, rising interest rates and continued selling pressure threaten a year-end recovery.

• *UBS Desk:* “Little indication that investors are eager to re-gross into year-end,” despite two major AI catalysts. Weak fund performance is discouraging renewed risk-taking.
• *Bank of America:* Michael Hartnett warns of a potential hard-landing feedback loop, where falling stocks trigger earnings downgrades, reduced allocations and further selling unless the Fed changes course.
• *Barclays:* Emmanuel Cau says investors increasingly fear the Fed will not rescue falling markets. Warns of further weakness if inflation stays hot, though AI investment demand remains intact.
• *Citi:* Dirk Willer's team warns its market-leadership risk indicator is nearing a sell signal, triggered when four of the seven largest S&P 500 stocks remain below their 200-day averages for five sessions.
• *Goldman Sachs Desk:* Analysts say no single headline caused the selloff, though AMD's China-related short-seller report further damaged already fragile AI sentiment.
• *Morningstar:* Michael Field says Anthropic's IPO briefly relieved negative sentiment, but “That pause is well and truly over unfortunately.”
• *Saxo:* Charu Chanana says investors now demand proof that massive AI spending can produce sustainable returns, not simply evidence of strong chip demand.
• *XTB:* Kathleen Brooks says hopes of an IPO-driven recovery “proved short lived,” citing Nvidia uncertainty, AI spending, higher rates and political changes.
• *Capital. com:* Daniela Hathorn says markets are entering a more defensive phase as strong AI demand and successful IPOs fail to offset valuation and financing concerns.

*U.S. stocks face monthly options expiration today, with heavy S&P 500, Nasdaq-100 and technology options positioning potentially amplifying volatility amid the market selloff.*

• *Market Setup:* SPX dealer gamma remains negative, according to third-party models, potentially amplifying both rallies and declines as dealers adjust hedges. GEX Metrix estimates -$33B per 1% move as of 8:30 AM ET.
• *Options Activity:* Thursday's tracked Nov. 20 put volume reached approximately 1.48M SPY, 952K QQQ, 863K Nvidia *($NVDA)* and 236K AMD *($AMD)* contracts, according to delayed SquawkFlow data.
• *Implied Volatility:* SPX options priced an approximately ±1.73% move (124 points) through Friday's close, based on Thursday's closing snapshot. This is a market-implied range, not a directional forecast.
• *Expiration Mechanics:* Standard monthly SPX options stopped trading Thursday and settle using Friday's opening stock prices. Equity, ETF and P.M.-settled index options expire Friday, potentially increasing hedging and rebalancing.
• *Historical Context:* The S&P 500 moved more than 1% on six of the first 10 monthly expiration days of 2026, although the small sample provides no reliable directional signal.

*Wall Street strategists warn that falling stocks, rising borrowing costs and slowing AI investment could force the Federal Reserve to reconsider further rate hikes. Bank of America, Citi and Barclays see growing risks to economic growth as tighter financial conditions collide with persistent inflation.*

• *Bank of America:* Michael Hartnett warns falling stocks and widening credit spreads could “short-circuit” Fed hikes. Continued tightening risks a hard landing, earnings downgrades and further selling.
• *Citi:* Calls current interest rates “unsustainably high,” warning the Fed has little appetite to hike into an equity selloff. Expects a 25-basis-point December hike, a pause in early 2027 and cuts later that year.
• *Barclays:* Emmanuel Cau warns investors fear the “Fed put has disappeared.” Slowing AI investment could weaken growth and reduce the need for aggressive tightening.
• *Standard Chartered:* Sees excessive tightening expectations, forecasting two more hikes before potential cuts in H2 2027 as oil prices ease. Also expects lower AI spending estimates.
• *JPMorgan:* Michael Feroli expects AI investment's contribution to growth to peak in 2026 and moderate in 2027, producing a manageable slowdown rather than a severe contraction.
• *Apollo Global:* Torsten Sløk estimates AI investment contributed roughly 65% of U.S. real GDP growth over the past three quarters before import adjustments, underscoring the economy's AI dependence.
• *Morgan Stanley:* Expects hikes to peak in Q1 2027, with AI spending supporting growth. Forecasts cuts in 2028, later than Citi.

TSMC *($TSM)* and Samsung have reportedly suspended certain chip shipments to Chinese customers following new U.S. export controls, with restrictions now affecting advanced AI processors and some consumer smartphone chips.

• *Manufacturing Restrictions:* Reuters reports TSMC halted affected Chinese orders using 16nm and more advanced processes without U.S. licenses. Some customers remain eligible for older 28nm and 40nm technology, excluding advanced packaging and high-bandwidth memory.
• *Export Controls:* New Commerce Department rules eliminate a previous compliance pathway using chip-design verification and restrict Chinese firms' access to advanced AI computing through overseas data centers.
• *Smartphone Impact:* Restrictions also affect processors supplied to Chinese brands including Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo. Industry sources expect consumer-chip licenses to be granted but warn approval delays could disrupt manufacturing.
